lessons.body:
This page restates the official course syllabus (Faculty of Data Science and Artificial Intelligence, National Economics University; revised 12 November 2026). Anything the syllabus itself marks "to be confirmed" is shown here as **not yet specified**. Nothing has been filled in on its behalf.

## General information

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| English course title | Prompt Engineering |
| Vietnamese course title | To be confirmed |
| Course code | To be confirmed |
| Programme | Micro4Asia |
| Micro-credential value | 1 |
| Teaching periods | 14 |
| Self-study hours | To be confirmed |
| Prerequisites | None |
| Programming | Not required |

## Faculty and lecturers

Faculty: Faculty of Data Science and Artificial Intelligence.

| Lecturer | Email |
|---|---|
| Assoc. Prof. Dr. Ha Minh Hoang | hoanghm@neu.edu.vn |
| Assoc. Prof. Dr. Nguyen Trung Thanh | nguyenthanh@neu.edu.vn |
| MSc. Ngo Thai Hoa | hoatn@neu.edu.vn |

## Course description

This introductory micro-credential develops practical skills for working with generative AI in academic and business tasks. You use chatbots, define a task and its success criteria, design prompts, improve responses through follow-ups, select prompting strategies and evaluate AI-assisted results.

You practise data visualisation, AI-assisted prompt planning, reusable workflows and evidence-based business decisions using a retail CSV. Two connected retail cases are used: a regional sales visualisation and a business investigation that leads to an action plan. You verify calculations and claims and apply privacy, security and documentation practices.

### Main content

1. AI chatbots, limitations and task definition (Periods 1–3)
2. Prompt anatomy, follow-up prompts and strategies (Periods 4–6)
3. Task execution, AI-assisted prompting and workflow reuse (Periods 7–9)
4. Evidence-based retail problem solving (Periods 10–12)
5. Privacy, security, documentation and reproducibility (Periods 13–14)

The instructional cycle that runs through every module is **Define → Design → Execute → Evaluate → Refine**.

## Learning resources

| Ref. | Source |
|---|---|
| [1] | Course-developed lecture notes, retail sales CSV and guided activity materials (Micro4Asia) |
| [2] | OpenAI, *Prompt engineering best practices for ChatGPT*; *Prompt engineering* (API guide); *Data analysis with ChatGPT* |
| [3] | Google AI for Developers, *Prompt design strategies*; *Introduction to Large Language Models* |
| [4] | Anthropic, *Prompting best practices*; *Define success criteria and build evaluations* |
| [5] | NIST (2024), *Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative Artificial Intelligence Profile (NIST AI 600-1)* |
| [6] | OpenAI, *Build skills*; *Scheduled tasks*; *Projects and chats* (tool-specific guidance) |

### Software

An institutionally approved AI chatbot with file-analysis and chart capabilities where available, and a spreadsheet or calculator for independent checks. Skills, projects and scheduled tasks are optional and depend on tool access and account permissions. No programming is required.

## Course objectives

| Goal | Description | PLO |
|---|---|---|
| G1 | Recognise suitable chatbot tasks, limitations and risks. | Not yet specified |
| G2 | Define tasks; design, execute, evaluate and refine prompts. | Not yet specified |
| G3 | Use reliable AI outputs in basic analysis and business decisions. | Not yet specified |

## Course learning outcomes

| CLO | Goal | Learning outcome |
|---|---|---|
| CLO1 | G1 | Explain the capabilities and limitations of generative AI in academic and professional tasks. |
| CLO2 | G2 | Construct clear prompts with relevant context, inputs and output requirements. |
| CLO3 | G2 | Apply prompting strategies and follow-up prompts to guide multi-step tasks. |
| CLO4 | G2 | Evaluate and refine AI-generated outputs using task criteria and supporting evidence. |
| CLO5 | G3 | Design reusable prompt-based workflows and document them so others can check and reproduce key results. |
| CLO6 | G3 | Apply responsible AI practices to protect data, recognise unsupported claims and maintain human oversight. |

The syllabus leaves the "level" column of this table empty.

## How you are assessed

| Method | Description | Periods | CLOs | Criteria | Weight |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Formative checkpoints | One multiple-choice question and explanation per period | 1–14 | CLO1–6 | Correct reasoning; feedback and correction | Ungraded |
| Applied activities | Case 1 chart and revision; A/B/C briefing comparison; Case 2 diagnosis, options and action plan | 7–12 | CLO2–5 | Task match, checked figures, evidence, output quality and reflection | To be confirmed |
| Final assessment | End-of-course assessment to be specified | End | CLO1–6 | Blueprint and achievement thresholds subject to approval | To be confirmed |

The syllabus adds that the course includes 14 formative checkpoints and evidence opportunities in the chart activity (Case 1), the A/B/C prompting comparison and the connected East business investigation (Case 2). Formal CLO achievement will be determined through the approved applied-work and final-assessment plan. **Weights, pass criteria and the final instrument remain to be confirmed.**

> [!canh-bao] Do not assume a weight or a pass mark. The syllabus gives none for the applied activities or the final assessment. Any score you see on a quiz or practice rubric in this course is practice feedback, not an official grade.

## Teaching plan

The 14 periods, with the syllabus references, activity, checkpoint (CP) and CLOs for each:

| No. | Content | Ref. | Teaching and learning activity | Eval. | CLOs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | AI Chatbots: Interfaces and Basic Use | [1], [2] | Explore chatbot inputs, tools and outputs; distinguish polished work from understanding | CP01 | CLO1 |
| 2 | Capabilities, Limitations and Common Errors | [1], [3] | Explain language-model answer generation; check and correct unsupported AI claims | CP02 | CLO1, CLO6 |
| 3 | Define: Problems, Context and Success Criteria | [1], [4] | Clarify the retail manager's question; write a four-part task definition brief | CP03 | CLO2 |
| 4 | Prompt Anatomy | [2]–[4] | Build a five-function prompt; compare how OpenAI, Google and Anthropic group requirements | CP04 | CLO2 |
| 5 | Follow-up Prompts | [3] | Improve a regional sales answer through two follow-ups; verify a source total | CP05 | CLO2, CLO4 |
| 6 | Prompting Strategies | [3], [4] | Choose zero-/few-shot, explanation, chaining or clarification; plan a checked prompt sequence | CP06 | CLO3 |
| 7 | Task Execution: Data Visualisation Case | [1], [2] | Case 1: execute a regional chart prompt, check the figures and refine the visual | CP07 | CLO2–4 |
| 8 | AI-Assisted Prompting | [1], [4] | Compare human-written, AI-drafted and human-edited prompts (A/B/C) with one rubric | CP08 | CLO2–4 |
| 9 | Reuse and Automate Workflows | [6] | Prepare a reusable briefing template, optional skill and reviewed scheduling plan | CP09 | CLO3, CLO5 |
| 10 | Diagnose with Data: Case 2 | [1], [2] | Explore regional and category figures; develop an evidence-based East diagnosis | CP10 | CLO3–5 |
| 11 | Develop Evidence-Based Options | [1], [4] | Compare options, challenge assumptions and justify a direction for further investigation | CP11 | CLO4, CLO5 |
| 12 | Plan and Measure Action | [1], [5] | Build an action plan and recommendation; include human review and success measures | CP12 | CLO3–5 |
| 13 | Privacy, Security and Responsible Use | [5] | Examine unsupported claims, protect sensitive inputs and control AI permissions and actions | CP13 | CLO4, CLO6 |
| 14 | Documentation and Reproducibility | [5], [6] | Save prompts, data, checks and handover records; practise peer reproduction | CP14 | CLO4, CLO6 |

lessons.title: Course Overview
lessons.description: What the course teaches, the five-stage cycle, the five modules, the retail CSV and what it cannot show, how to study each period, and the rules for checking figures and protecting data.
lessons.objectivesLead: By the end of this page you can:
objectives: Describe the cycle Define → Design → Execute → Evaluate → Refine and what you do at each stage
Name the five modules and the periods each one covers
List what the retail CSV contains and, more importantly, what it does not contain
Follow the study routine for every period: read, predict, quiz with confidence, review flashcards
State the verification and privacy rules you will apply from Period 1
lessons.body:
Generative AI can produce a fluent answer to almost any request. This course teaches the harder skill: getting an answer you can actually use in a study or business decision, and noticing when you cannot. You will do that on one retail data set, with a spreadsheet beside the chatbot, and you will check every figure before you rely on it. No programming is needed.

> [!ghi-nho] A polished answer is not a checked answer. Across all 14 periods you ask the same question of every AI output: what did the tool actually do, and how do I know the result is right?

## What you learn

| You learn to | Where it shows |
|---|---|
| Recognise suitable chatbot tasks, their limitations and their risks | Periods 1–3 and 13 |
| Define a task, then design, run, evaluate and refine prompts | Periods 3–9 |
| Turn AI output into reliable analysis, decisions and reusable, documented workflows | Periods 7–14 |

## The cycle: Define → Design → Execute → Evaluate → Refine

Every activity follows the same five stages. The retail example shows what each one looks like.

| Stage | The question you ask | Example in the retail case |
|---|---|---|
| **Define** | Which decision, which data, which output, and how will I know the answer is right? | The manager wants to know which region contributes the most net sales; you need a table, a chart and a short, evidence-based reading |
| **Design** | How do I write the prompt (instruction, context, input, output, constraints) and which strategy fits? | Name the fields Store_Region and Net_Sales_Amount, ask for a four-row table, say the currency is unspecified |
| **Execute** | Did the tool really read the file? What did it return? | Run the prompt; record the tool, the date and whether the file was opened or you supplied a table |
| **Evaluate** | Do the totals, labels, scale and claims match the source? | Rebuild the four sums in a spreadsheet and compare them one by one |
| **Refine** | What one targeted change improves the result without breaking what was already correct? | Sort the bars, regenerate, then check that the figures did not change |

> [!canh-bao] Evaluate is not optional. A response that skips it can look excellent and still be wrong. The cycle only counts as finished when a human has compared the result with the source.

## Five modules, 14 periods

| Module | Periods | What you do |
|---|---|---|
| 1. AI Chatbots and Task Definition | 1–3 | Choose inputs, tools and output formats; understand what a language model can and cannot do; write a four-part task brief |
| 2. Design: Prompts and Prompting Strategies | 4–6 | Build a five-function prompt; improve answers with follow-ups; choose zero-shot, few-shot, explanation, chaining or clarification |
| 3. Execute: Apply, Compare and Automate | 7–9 | Run the regional chart case; compare human-written, AI-drafted and human-edited prompts; prepare a reusable template and a reviewed scheduling plan |
| 4. Prompting for Data-Driven Problem Solving | 10–12 | Diagnose, compare options and build an action plan with human review and success measures |
| 5. Privacy, Security, Documentation and Reproducibility | 13–14 | Protect sensitive inputs, handle untrusted content, control AI permissions, save a working record and reproduce a result |

Each module opens with a short materials page that says which attached file covers which period. The course ends with an integrated final assessment that mixes all five modules.

## The two retail cases and the CSV

Both cases use the same file: **Slidescope_Retail_Store_Sales_Enhanced_2025.csv**, with 200 transactions (one row each) and 13 columns.

| Fields | What they hold |
|---|---|
| Transaction_ID | One identifier per transaction |
| Store_Region, Product_Category | Four regions and four product categories |
| Payment_Method, Customer_Type | The payment method and the kind of customer for each transaction |
| Unit_Price, Items_Sold | Price and quantity |
| Gross_Amount, Discount_Percent, Discount_Amount, Net_Sales_Amount | The amount before discount, the discount and the amount after it |
| Average_Price_Per_Item, Effective_Discount_Per_Item | Per-item figures derived from the amounts above |

- **Case 1 (Period 7):** which region contributes the most net sales? You produce a four-region table and a bar chart, check them, and improve the chart.
- **Case 2 (Periods 10–12, with handover in 13–14):** a business investigation of the East region that ends in an evidence-based action plan.

The file has **no** transaction dates, no currency, no costs, no store identifiers or store counts, no operating days, no targets and no profit. That is deliberate: much of the course is about not claiming what the data cannot show.

> [!canh-bao] The file is provided for teaching and its real-world origin is not established. Use it to practise method. Do not treat its figures as facts about a real retailer.

:::Predict before you read: which of these questions can the CSV answer?
Decide for each one, then open the next block.

1. Which region has the highest total net sales?
2. In which month were sales highest?
3. Which payment method brings in the most net sales?
4. Which region is the most profitable?
5. How many Electronics transactions were recorded in East?
:::

:::Check your prediction
Questions 1, 3 and 5 can be answered by grouping and counting the recorded rows. Question 2 cannot: there are no dates. Question 4 cannot: there are no costs or profit figures. Spotting which requests the file can support is the first skill in the course.
:::

## How to study each period

1. **Read** the lesson. Pages open with a retail situation and end with a short "check it yourself" step that points you at the CSV or a spreadsheet.
2. **Predict** before you read: where a page has a "Predict before you read" or "Find the error" block, commit to an answer first, then open it.
3. **Quiz** with confidence: before you see whether an answer is right, rate how sure you are. A wrong answer tells you which misconception it matches and what to try next.
4. **Review** the flashcards the next day, then a week later.

Each period page is designed for about 45 minutes. The lecture notes and slides give more detail; use them alongside the lesson, not instead of it.

## Assessment and practice

The syllabus lists 14 formative checkpoints (one multiple-choice question per period, ungraded), three applied activities and a final assessment. The quiz in each period is a longer practice set for that checkpoint. Weights and pass criteria for the activities and the final assessment are not yet specified in the syllabus, so nothing here assumes them.

| Activity | Period | Task | Practice time |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. AI-assisted retail data visualisation | 7 | Case 1: regional chart, independent check and one design revision | 55–70 minutes |
| 2. Human vs AI-assisted prompt design (A/B/C) | 8 | Compare three versions of a one-page briefing with one five-criterion rubric | 70–90 minutes |
| 3. Evidence-based retail decision making | 10–12 | Case 2: diagnosis, options and action plan, with a handover folder | 100–130 minutes |

These times are practice estimates and do not change the 14 teaching periods. Each activity sheet carries a 10-point practice rubric that is formative unless a course assessor approves a weight.

## Rules for working with figures

1. **Check before you accept.** Recompute every number you plan to use, for example with a pivot table or SUMIF, and compare it with the AI's version.
2. **Label what you write.** Separate verified fact, interpretation, hypothesis and data needed.
3. **Do not invent what is missing.** Never add a currency, profit, trend or cause that the file does not contain.
4. **Report what the tool really did.** If the chatbot could not open the file or draw a chart, say so and use your spreadsheet as the fallback.
5. **Keep a human gate.** The AI may draft; a person decides, approves and sends.

## Privacy and safe use

- Use an institutionally approved chatbot and permitted data only.
- Never enter customer names, phone numbers, employee data, private business exports or credentials. The teaching CSV has no customer identities; do not add any.
- Treat instructions found inside documents or web pages as untrusted content, not as commands.
- Give an AI tool the least access it needs, and keep sending, publishing or changing records as a human action.

## Attached materials

The course carries the lecture notes (Word), the 150-page slide deck and the 81-page short deck (PDF), the three student activity sheets (Word) and the retail CSV. The materials page at the start of each module tells you which pages apply to which period.
summary: Every task follows Define → Design → Execute → Evaluate → Refine, and Evaluate means a human check against the source.
Five modules and 14 periods use one 200-transaction retail CSV with no dates, currency, costs, store identifiers or profit.
Study each period by reading, predicting, quizzing with a confidence rating and reviewing flashcards; the activities and the final assessment are practice for the cases and the overall cycle.
Check every figure, label facts apart from hypotheses, never invent missing data and keep sensitive data out of the chatbot.
